newsitem.title: UK: IPE Brent, gas oil turn lower as Iraq rally fades.
newsitem.headline: IPE Brent, gas oil turn lower as Iraq rally fades.

text.p: IPE Brent crude and gas oil turned lower late Tuesday as dealers took profits after an early rally inspired by U.S. military action against Iraq and as both contracts found little technical support.

September gas oil, which posted a session high of $212.50 a tonne, closed down $3.25 at $204.50. At 1646 GMT, Oct Brent was down 14 cents at $21.85 a barrel after sinking as low as $21.57 in mid-afternoon trade.
"Gas oil kept in line with Brent today. There was pretty good volume but it was hard to find bids on the way down," said a broker.

IPE Oct Brent touched a high of $22.85 a barrel on news of a U.S. cruise missile attack against air defence installations in the south of Iraq but the rally faded as it became clear there was no imminent threat to Mideast oil supplies.

Both contract were vulnerable to a sharp retracement after leaving chart gaps during Monday's rally after the U.N. said it was postponing the May 20 oil-for-food deal with Iraq in reponse to Baghdad's attacks on Kurdish safe areas in the north.
Brent crude remained $1 above Friday's closing levels and European spot crude markets were also drawing strength from the indefinite delays to the resumption of Iraqi exports.

U.S. envoy to the U.N. Edward Gnehm said the terms of the deal would have to be reopened in the wake of Baghdad's latest military action and it could take "months and months" for the deal to be implemented.
Oil analysts and traders said they were not expecting to see the first Iraqi crude exports since the Gulf War this side of Christmas.
The Oct Brent-gas oil crack eased back slightly from early levels, closing at $5.08 a barrel from $5.30 on Tuesday morning.
